How Apple Animoji works — and why listing copy is a separate job

Teams assume Animoji support in the iOS binary covers storefront language. Animoji picker, Messages recording, FaceTime presentation, and App Store Connect actually separate on-device Animoji behavior from product-page copy:

  • Animoji picker (动话表情选择器) — system UI in Messages or FaceTime where buyers choose preset animal and character faces — panda, monkey, unicorn, robot, alien, and similar. Does not generate Chinese listing text by itself.
  • Animoji in Messages (信息动话表情) — record a short Animoji video message that tracks facial expressions and send it in a chat thread. Gallery frames may show record button, character grid, or send preview — listing copy should use 动话表情 or Messages 动话表情 when that is what the screenshot depicts.
  • Animoji in FaceTime (FaceTime 动话表情) — replace the camera feed with an animated Animoji character that tracks expressions during a video call. Marketing may show FaceTime Animoji tiles — caption lines should name FaceTime 动话表情 or 动态表情 when art shows motion tracking.
  • Expression tracking (动态表情) — eyebrow raise, mouth open, head tilt, and blink mirrored on the preset character face through TrueDepth sensors. Distinct from Reaction Effects gesture confetti unless your English gallery already shows that specific overlay UI.
  • Preset characters vs Memoji editor — Animoji uses Apple's built-in animal and character roster; Memoji lets buyers customize a personalized avatar. This page leads preset Animoji animals — 动话表情 — not Memoji editor skin-and-hair personalization as the hero.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Animoji features in the binary.

Working Animoji workflows on device and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
